methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous multiomics integration study combining ex vivo DSP (n=81 pediatric solid tumors) with genomic/transcriptomic data using MOFA+ factor analysis. Comprehensive bioinformatics pipeline: variant calling (WES), CNV analysis (CNVkit), RNA-seq (STAR/featureCounts), gene fusion detection (Arriba). MOFA+ model trained with variance threshold 2%, convergence threshold 0.01. Factor selection criteria well-defined (≥10% drug response variance). Validation via TARGET cohort (Wilms tumors, n=101) and GDSC2 (neuroblastoma cell lines). Appropriate multivariate statistical approaches.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Translational study identifying biomarkers (SIX1 mutation, MGAM/PTPN14/STAT4/KDM2B expression) associated with MEKi sensitivity in pediatric Wilms tumor subset. LoE 5: functional precision medicine combining DSP/omics without prospective clinical validation. Clinical relevance: preliminary biomarker identification for treatment stratification; requires functional validation and clinical trial before impact.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods including ex vivo DSP protocol, sequencing workflows, and bioinformatics pipelines clearly detailed. MOFA+ parameters explicitly specified. Supplementary figures extensively document clustering, pathway analyses, and CARNIVAL network results. No statement on code/data availability; INFORM registry data subject to institutional access restrictions.

novelty_literature.justification: First integrated analysis linking drug sensitivity profiling + multiomics in pediatric solid tumors using MOFA+. Identification of SIX1 (Q177R) mutation associated with MEKi sensitivity in Wilms tumors novel and clinically actionable. Mechanistic network analysis (CARNIVAL) linking SIX1-AKT1-MAPK14-ETS1 pathway innovative. Addresses documented gap in pediatric precision medicine biomarkers.

writing_presentation.justification: Exceptionally well-written with clear methodology and logical presentation flow. Figures effectively communicate MOFA+ factor contributions, drug sensitivity clustering, and pathway networks. Discussion appropriately addresses limitations and calls for functional validation. Mechanistic insights well-articulated despite complexity.

key_strengths: Novel integrated DSP + multiomics approach (MOFA+) identifying MEKi-sensitive Wilms tumor subset with SIX1 hotspot mutation
Independent validation in TARGET cohort (n=101) confirming SIX1 association with MGAM/STAT4/KDM2B expression (P<0.004)
Mechanistic CARNIVAL network analysis linking SIX1 mutation to MEK pathway sensitivity via AKT1-ETS1
Addresses critical unmet need: pediatric solid tumor biomarkers for MEK/CDK inhibitors largely lacking
key_concerns: Small discovery cohort (only 3 SIX1-mutant Wilms tumors with MEKi sensitivity) limits robustness of signature
CARNIVAL network analysis computational; requires functional validation (knockdown/overexpression) to confirm SIX1/AKT/MEK interactions
GDSC2 validation shows BCL2 sensitivity and gene expression independent in neuroblastoma, questioning signature predictiveness
No prospective clinical trial data; findings hypothesis-generating requiring functional studies and clinical validation
Limited generalizability: pediatric-specific, rare tumor types (only 4 SIX1 mutants in TARGET validation)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Innovative integrative omics study with rigorous statistical methodology identifying clinically actionable pediatric cancer biomarker. Appropriate for Tier 2 publication with functional validation as next step. Minor revisions needed emphasizing hypothesis-generating nature and functional validation requirements.
